title: Generic-point full faithfulness for finite etale covers of a normal integral scheme
statement: Let B be an integral scheme with integrally closed local rings [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. For finite etale πX:X → B and πY:Y → B, let Xη and Yη be any cartesian restrictions to Spec K(B), with projections πXη, πYη and comparison maps ψX, ψY [def-pc-fibre-product]. Every morphism fη:Xη → Yη satisfying fη;πYη=πXη admits a unique f:X → Y such that f;πY=πX and ψX;f=fη;ψY. The covers may be empty or disconnected. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BQM, full faithfulness in the proof; Tag 0BQL, normalization of finite etale covers

proof.text: On a nonempty affine open Spec A of B, A is an integrally closed domain. Finite etale covers correspond to finite etale A-algebras, which are normal and are the integral closures of A in their generic finite products of separable field extensions (0BQL, componentwise). A generic A-algebra homomorphism preserves integrality over A, so it restricts to a homomorphism of these finite etale A-algebras, with the contravariant direction appropriate for scheme morphisms. This constructs the extension on every affine chart.

Finite etale A-algebras are flat, hence torsion free over the domain A, and embed into their generic algebras. Any two local extensions with the same generic restriction therefore coincide. Restricting affine-chart maps to a common affine refinement of an overlap gives equality, so the maps glue. The same injectivity proves global uniqueness. Arbitrary cartesian presentations of the generic restrictions are identified by their unique pullback isomorphisms, giving the displayed comparison equation. The zero algebra handles empty covers.
